content.text:
Tout est propre côté sandbox : un seul worktree, main à 6109ff2, rien qui traîne.

Sur l'hôte, il te reste une seule chose — supprimer le répertoire résiduel que ma suppression n'atteint pas (il est hors du montage, dans ta couche à toi) :

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force ..\devdesk-feat-oci-pull-job
git worktree prune -v
git status

Le .worktrees/ a déjà disparu de ton côté, lui, puisqu'il était dans le montage.

Ce qui s'est passé avec ton git worktree remove, et c'est une découverte qui manque à la doc que je viens d'écrire : .worktrees/ partage les fichiers entre hôte et sandbox, mais pas l'enregistrement git. Un worktree créé dans la sandbox inscrit un chemin Linux (/c/Users/...) que ton git Windows ne résout pas — d'où « is not a working tree ». Pire : ton git worktree prune de l'étape 1 l'a désenregistré en silence, le jugeant disparu, tout en laissant le worktree frère dont le chemin C:/... lui parlait.

Conséquence pratique : celui qui crée un worktree est celui qui doit le retirer. Ça ne t'a rien coûté ici (le contenu était déjà mergé), mais un prune de l'hôte pendant que je travaille dans un worktree désenregistrerait le mien sous mes pieds.

Ma modification de .claude/CLAUDE.md (mergée en #165) ne dit pas ça — je ne l'avais pas encore observé. Veux-tu que j'ajoute ce paragraphe dans une petite PR de suivi ? C'est le genre de piège qui ne se retrouve qu'en le revivant.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
7	> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
8	>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
9	> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
10	>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
11	>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`.
12	> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
13	>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
14	>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.
15	
16	## Project Overview
17	
18	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
19	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
20	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
21	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
22	- Docker container management with real-time metrics
23	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
24	- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces
25	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
26	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
27	
28	## Build and Development Commands
29	
30	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
31	
32	```bash
33	# Development (fastest)
34	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
35	go run .
36	
37	# Build
38	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
39	mise run run          # Build and run
40	
41	# Testing
42	mise run test         # Run all tests
43	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
44	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
45	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
46	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
47	
48	# Code Quality
49	mise run fmt          # Format code
50	mise run vet          # Run go vet
51	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
52	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
53	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
54	
55	# Installation
56	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
57	```
58	
59	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
60	
61	## Work starts in a new worktree
62	
63	**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
64	the current `main`, **under `.worktrees/` inside the repository**:
65	
66	```bash
67	git fetch origin main
68	git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main
69	cd .worktrees/<branch>
70	```

input.pattern: Landing a sandbox-made commit|What isolates, and what does not|worktree remove refuses a tree

result.output:
70	```
71	
72	Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
73	Editing does.
74	
75	**Under the repository, not beside it.** This reverses what this file said until
76	now, and the reason it gave was wrong. It claimed a worktree at `.worktrees/x`
77	would be compiled by `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`. It would not: the go
78	tool skips every directory whose name begins with `.` or `_`, so `.worktrees/`
79	is invisible to `./...`. Verified rather than assumed — a package of deliberately
80	invalid Go placed under `.worktrees/` builds clean and `go list ./...` does not
81	name it. The old argument holds for `worktrees/` without the dot, which is
82	presumably where it came from.
83	
84	What decides it is the **sandbox mount**, and it cost a full debugging session to
85	find. A direct-mode sandbox mounts *this directory only*. A sibling worktree at
86	`../devdesk-<branch>` is therefore outside the mount, so its **files** are written
87	into the container's private layer and never reach the host — while `.git` is
88	inside the mount and stays shared. Refs agree, files diverge, and nothing warns:
89	the branch tip moves, the host's copy of those files does not, and `git status`
90	on the host reports the *stale* content as uncommitted modifications. An agent
91	and the person testing its work end up compiling different code while both
92	believe they are on the same branch. Under `.worktrees/`, host and sandbox see
93	one filesystem.
94	
95	Two effects worth knowing, neither blocking:
96	
97	- `.worktrees/` is in `.gitignore`; a worktree there is not a change to the tree.
98	- Claude Code discovers the nested `.claude/` of each worktree, so its skills and
99	  rules appear a second time, prefixed by the worktree path. Harmless, and the
100	  price of the directory being inside the repo.
101	
102	**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
103	worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
104	whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:
105	
106	| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
107	|---|---|
108	| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
109	| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
110	| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
111	| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |
112	
113	`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.
114	
115	**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
116	first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
117	and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
118	(`local/<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the first search
119	being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.
120	
121	**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:
122	
123	```bash
124	git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
125	git worktree list          # what is still out there
126	git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
127	```
128	
129	`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
130	point — look before forcing.
131	
132	**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
133	origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
134	every new worktree is cut from.
135	
136	## Git workflow — pull requests only
137	
138	**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:
139	
140	```
141	! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
142	```
143	
144	This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
145	— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
146	The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
147	forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.
148	
149	What rules GitHub out is that branch protection is *unavailable* on this
150	repository: it is private on a free personal plan, so both endpoints answer
151	`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` —
152	`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and `/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets`
153	alike. Do not cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting
154	`"protected": false` as the proof: that field only ever reflects legacy branch
155	protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and on this plan it would
156	read `false` whatever the configuration. The 403 is the evidence; the `false` is
157	not.
158	
159	Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
160	and is forwarded to GitHub.
161	
162	**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
163	concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
164	the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
165	to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
166	branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.
167	
168	```bash
169	git worktree add -b <branch> .worktrees/<branch> origin/main   # work happens here
170	git push -u origin <branch>                     # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
171	gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
172	gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
173	# then, from the main checkout:
174	git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
175	git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
176	```
177	
178	**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
179	remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
180	finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
181	repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
182	Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.
183	
184	**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
185	GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
186	`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
187	says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
188	it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
189	because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.
190	
191	**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** It would
192	be the one path that defeats the only protection there is: `main` cannot be
193	protected on GitHub here (see the 403 above), so the mirror's refusal is the
194	whole of it, and `git push github main` would simply succeed. A direct push also
195	bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that records checkpoints and
196	sessions — which is not visible until much later. `origin` is the only remote,
197	deliberately.
198	
199	**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
200	`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
201	second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
202	keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.
203	
204	### Landing a sandbox-made commit (host-relay)
205	
206	A Docker Sandbox (`sbx`) has no `entire://` auth of its own — `ENTIRE_TOKEN`
207	via `sbx secret set-custom` doesn't work (`git-remote-entire` parses the
208	JWT's claims locally, before any network call, but the secret proxy only
209	substitutes the real token on the wire — the sandbox process itself only
210	ever sees an unparseable placeholder), and an interactive `entire login`
211	inside the sandbox trades that for a persistent, harder-to-reason-about
212	credential sitting in a less-trusted place. So the sandbox edits and commits
213	locally only; the host does every `origin` operation — fetch, push, PR,
214	merge. `git pull`/`git fetch` run *inside* the sandbox will fail with `no
215	auth context for cluster ...` — that's expected, not a setup bug; don't
216	`entire login` there to fix it (see `~/projects/github/anthnel/sbx-kits/entire/README.md`
217	for the full rationale).
218	
219	A direct-mode sandbox mounts this exact repo directory, so both the commits and
220	the working files land where the host sees them — provided the worktree is under
221	`.worktrees/`, which is why that is the rule. There is nothing to transfer; the
222	host only has to push, because the sandbox has no `entire://` auth:
223	
224	```bash
225	# From the host, once the sandbox reports "done and committed":
226	git push origin <branch>
227	gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch> --fill
228	gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
229	git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see above

229	git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see above
230	git worktree remove .worktrees/<branch>
231	```
232	
233	**If a worktree was made at the old sibling path** (`../devdesk-<branch>`), the
234	host cannot see its files and `git worktree list` shows it `prunable`. The
235	commits are still in the shared `.git/objects`, so nothing is lost — but the
236	host's copy of those files is stale, and `git status` there reports that stale
237	content as uncommitted modifications, which reads as if work were pending when
238	the opposite is true. Recover by taking the branch tip:
239	
240	```bash
241	git stash push -m "stale files from a sandbox sibling worktree"   # reversible
242	git worktree prune -v                  # drop the unreachable admin entry
243	git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>
244	```
245	
246	**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
247	squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
248	history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
249	(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
250	landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
251	through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
252	instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
253	clean:
254	
255	```bash
256	git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> .worktrees/<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
257	cd .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
258	git reset --hard origin/main
259	git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
260	go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
261	git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
262	# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
263	git worktree remove .worktrees/<tmp-branch>
264	```
265	
266	### Remotes
267	
268	| Remote | URL | Use |
269	|--------|-----|-----|
270	| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |
271	
272	**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on
273	GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1` (a second placement exists
274	in `aws-us-east-2`), but every git operation goes through the mirror: it is the
275	regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint
276	hook runs. Anything needing GitHub's own answer — PR state, review threads —
277	goes through `gh`, which authenticates directly and does not need a remote.
278	
279	Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
280	**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
281	yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
282	fixes this.
283

```bash
git stash push -m "stale files from a sandbox sibling worktree"   # reversible
git worktree prune -v                  # drop the unreachable admin entry
git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>
```

**A worktree created from inside the sandbox registers a Linux path the
host's git can't resolve — even under `.worktrees/`.** `.worktrees/` shares
*files* between host and sandbox, but each side's git still writes its own
`.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir` pointer, and the sandbox's git records a Linux
path (`/c/Users/...`). The host's `git worktree remove` on that same
directory then fails with `fatal: '<path>' is not a working tree` — Windows
git cannot resolve the pointer left behind. The costlier part: a plain `git
worktree prune` run on the host right after that failure deregisters the
worktree **silently** — git treats an unresolvable pointer as a worktree
that's gone — while leaving alone any sibling worktree whose path it *can*
read. If the branch was already merged the content is safe either way, but a
host-run `prune` while an agent is still working inside a sandbox-created
worktree would deregister that worktree out from under it, mid-task, with
nothing on either side raising a warning. The rule this implies: **whoever
creates a worktree removes it** — do not `git worktree remove` or `prune`
from the other side of the host/sandbox split.
